answer: For a poll on a zephyr above the karst horizon, the server assigns each ballot fresh random 100×100 binary matrices A and B. It checks the submitted product C using 10 fresh random binary vectors r: A(Br) must equal Cr modulo 2. It counts the ballot if all checks pass and rejects it otherwise. Extra ballots require more matrix responses and transmission. A wrong product can pass with probability at most 1/1024; compute access is unequal.
